summary: Equip yourself with essential knowledge on evidence handling and admissibility in financial crime cases. Sign up for our specialized training course today.
lede: Evidence handling and admissibility in financial crime cases involve preserving and documenting material so its integrity can be assessed. Designed for investigators, compliance and audit professionals, prosecutors, and litigation teams, the course covers mapping evidence sources, preserving physical and digital records, maintaining chain-of-custody logs, and preparing indexed exhibits and investigation reports.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for a wide range of professionals involved in financial crime investigations and compliance.
modules: Foundations of Evidence in Financial Crime Cases
Mapping Evidence Sources in Financial Crime Investigations
Securing and Preserving Evidence Without Contamination
Chain of Custody That Holds Up Under Challenge
Digital Evidence Handling for Non-Forensics Professionals
Evidence Documentation and Case File Discipline
Handling Financial Records and Analytical Outputs
Common Admissibility Challenges and How to Reduce Risk
Evidence Handling in Internal Investigations and Disciplinary Hearings
Preparing Evidence Bundles for Regulators and Court Processes
Governance, Privacy, and Ethical Evidence Handling
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of financial crime investigation processes and be familiar with general legal and compliance frameworks.
